#Budget for your safe. Wall safes cost between $50-$350 on average but some will be even higher priced. For a decent safe you can budget between $150-300 but the actual price will depend on the features and size you want.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 1 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Figure out the correct size. Most homes are built from two-by-fours (44 x 94mm) spaced 16 inches (40.5 cm) apart. This means that the typical safe will have to fit in this space. Look for a wall safe with a width of less than 16 inches (40.5 cm) and depth of 3.5 inches (9 cm). You can then chose the height that you prefer in which to fit your belongings.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 2 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#[[Choose a Wall Safe|Choose a wall safe]] with fire resistance. Fire resistant safes will protect your valuables and papers in the event of a fire. Both Underwriters Laboratories (UL)<ref>https://www.ul.com/news/personal-safe-sales-rise-how-safe-are-they</ref> and Intertek (ETL) <ref>https://www.intertek.com/marks/etl/</ref> are independent organizations that rate wall safes according to fire resistance. If you want a fire resistant wall safe choose one that will protect your goods for at least 30 minutes because most fires move through a room in about 20 minutes.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 3 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Decide which access control features you would like. Access control features may include a combination, a key, both a key and pin code or biometric data such as a fingerprint. All access methods are fairly effective and depend on the user to maintain their effectiveness.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 4 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Check theft resistance ratings. Some but not all wall safes have been tested for burglary resistance. Again check for the UL label. A safe rated B4 then it would be able to withstand an attack of at least 15 minutes using common tools.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 5 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Decide if you want water resistance. Water resistance ratings are also performed by Intertek and will be marked “verified” if they meet criteria. These safes would protect valuables in case of a flood or broken water line.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Buy your safe from a store that specializes in safes. Safes can be purchased from many hardware stores as well as online marketplaces. Buying a wall safe from a shop that specializes in safes can give you the opportunity to speak to an expert regarding the options that would work best for you.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Find the right location. Choose a location that is accessible so that you can use the safe effectively. Additionally the safe should be out of the regular traffic pattern of the house such as a closet, the laundry room, behind a heavy piece of furniture, behind a bookcase filled with books or in a child’s room. This makes the wall safe less noticeable and obvious to potential intruders.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Locate your studs. <ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5YKmNDmKXVo</ref> You will want to fix your safe between studs to allow it to be recessed inside your wall and thus less noticeable. Use a stud finder to [[Find a Stud|locate the studs]] behind the wall by running the stud finder across your wall. The tool will have an indicator to show when it has found a stud.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Mark your studs. Use a pencil to mark the locations of the studs on the wall. This will help orient your lines when you cut out the section of the wall.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Cut out a small square of space using a drywall saw.<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/home-safety/21016342/how-to-install-a-wall-safe</ref> After you’ve found a good safe and a place to install it between studs, you are ready to cut into your wall. Cut out a small square of space big enough for your hand to fit through.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 11 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Reach into the space with your hand to feel for electrical wiring or plumbing. If you find wires you need to be extra careful to go around them or reroute them. If you find plumbing in the way you may need to find a new location. If the wall is clear, you are ready to cut out a space for your safe.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 12 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Measure the wall to mark the size hole needing to be cut for the safe. Mark the four corners of your square hole using a pencil. Use a level to make level lines between the four corners. It is essential that the top and bottom are parallel with the ground while the sides are parallel with your studs.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 13 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Cut along the marks to create a hole in the wall. Use your drywall saw to cut along the marked lines. Start with the bottom edge of the opening and then cut the sides. You should cut the top line last to make sure the piece does not fall out beforehand, creating an uneven line.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 14 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Slide your safe into the hole. Put your safe into the hole, remembering to keep it help up with your hand. The door is the heaviest part of the safe due to the locking mechanism so be careful to hold up the corner so that it doesn’t fall out on you.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 15 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Fix the safe to the studs by drilling through the holes in the sides of the safe. Drill holes into the sides that match with the holes on the interior of your safe. Drill in each screw and then tighten them firmly.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 16 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Insert the shelves. Place the shelves inside the safe in their desired locations, making sure you line them up correctly. Some shelves will have cutouts to make space for the door locking mechanism and door hinges; make sure these cutouts are in the correct locations.[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 17 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Choose the wall safe with a fire protection rating according to what you would like to protect. Papers should not get hotter than 350 degrees F (176 degrees C), old tape recordings or 35mm slides no hotter than 150 degrees F (65 degrees C) and CDs/DVDs no hotter than 125 degrees F (52 degrees C).<ref>http://www.consumerreports.org/cro/2011/01/choosing-and-using-a-home-safe/index.htm</ref>
#*In Europe the Eurograde system evaluates wall safes.

#Decide which access control features you would like. Access control features may include a combination, a key, both a key and pin code or biometric data such as a fingerprint. All access methods are fairly effective and depend on the user to maintain their effectiveness.
#*If you are using a wall safe as a gun safe then it might be preferable to choose biometric access to prevent a key or code from falling into the hands of children.

#Check theft resistance ratings. Some but not all wall safes have been tested for burglary resistance. Again check for the UL label. A safe rated B4 then it would be able to withstand an attack of at least 15 minutes using common tools.
#*Most burglaries take around 8-12 minutes so a wall safe with this rating would be safe during this time.
#*Ratings of B1, B2 or B3 mean the safe provides very little security and resistance to tools.

#*A B5 rating means the safe can withstand 30 minutes of a typical attack with common tools while a B6 rating means the safe can withstand 30 minutes of attack with common tools, torches and carbide-tipped tools.<ref>http://www.consumerreports.org/cro/2011/01/choosing-and-using-a-home-safe/index.htm</ref>

#Decide if you want water resistance. Water resistance ratings are also performed by Intertek and will be marked “verified” if they meet criteria. These safes would protect valuables in case of a flood or broken water line.

#Buy your safe from a store that specializes in safes. Safes can be purchased from many hardware stores as well as online marketplaces. Buying a wall safe from a shop that specializes in safes can give you the opportunity to speak to an expert regarding the options that would work best for you.

#Find the right location. Choose a location that is accessible so that you can use the safe effectively. Additionally the safe should be out of the regular traffic pattern of the house such as a closet, the laundry room, behind a heavy piece of furniture, behind a bookcase filled with books or in a child’s room. This makes the wall safe less noticeable and obvious to potential intruders.
#*The location will also depend on the studs in your wall. Make sure you choose a location which will be able to make use of the space between studs.
=== Installing a Wall Safe ===

#Locate your studs. You will want to fix your safe between studs to allow it to be recessed inside your wall and thus less noticeable. Use a stud finder to [[Find a Stud|locate the studs]] behind the wall by running the stud finder across your wall. The tool will have an indicator to show when it has found a stud.

[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 1.jpg|center|550px]]
#* Stud finders can be purchased from your local hardware store.

#* If you don’t have a stud finder you can knock on the wall and listen for a hollow or solid sound. If the sound is hollow then the location is probably between studs; if it sounds solid then there is likely a stud in this location.
#*Knock a nail into the wall. As you hammer you will be able to feel if you hit a stud by the way the nail goes into the wall. These holes will be covered once you have installed your wall safe.
#Mark your studs. Use a pencil to mark the locations of the studs on the wall. This will help orient your lines when you cut out the section of the wall.

#Cut out a small square of space using a drywall saw. After you’ve found a good safe and a place to install it between studs, you are ready to cut into your wall. Cut out a small square of space big enough for your hand to fit through.

[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 3.jpg|center|550px]]

#Reach into the space with your hand to feel for electrical wiring or plumbing. If you find wires you need to be extra careful to go around them or reroute them. If you find plumbing in the way you may need to find a new location. If the wall is clear, you are ready to cut out a space for your safe.

#Measure the wall to mark the size hole needing to be cut for the safe. Mark the four corners of your square hole using a pencil. Use a level to make level lines between the four corners. It is essential that the top and bottom are parallel with the ground while the sides are parallel with your studs.

[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 4.jpg|center|550px]]
#* Make sure to measure and level correctly so that you don’t end up with an uneven or wrongly sized hole.

#Cut along the marks to create a hole in the wall. Use your drywall saw to cut along the marked lines. Start with the bottom edge of the opening and then cut the sides. You should cut the top line last to make sure the piece does not fall out beforehand, creating an uneven line.

# Slide your safe into the hole. Put your safe into the hole, remembering to keep it help up with your hand. The door is the heaviest part of the safe due to the locking mechanism so be careful to hold up the corner so that it doesn’t fall out on you.

#Fix the safe to the studs by drilling through the holes in the sides of the safe. Drill holes into the sides that match with the holes on the interior of your safe. Drill in each screw and then tighten them firmly.

[[Image:Install a Wall Safe Step 5.jpg|center|550px]]
#*This is an important step that prevents burglars from simply cutting your safe out of the wall and walking away with the whole thing.

#Insert the shelves. Place the shelves inside the safe in their desired locations, making sure you line them up correctly. Some shelves will have cutouts to make space for the door locking mechanism and door hinges; make sure these cutouts are in the correct locations.

*You may need to put a support for beneath the safe. Cut a piece of two-by-four (44 x 94 mm) wood to the exact length as the space between the studs. Screw these pieces diagonally into the studs on each side. This provides extra support for the base of the safe but is an optional step.
* Installing a wall safe can be quick and simple. However, if you have little handiwork experience, consult an experienced (and trusted) handyman.

added: A wall safe can be a handy way to hide away valuables in a secure place. Installing a safe is a relatively simple home project. However, if you install it incorrectly, it can be more trouble than it’s worth. Criminals can simply cut out an improperly installed safe and take it with them. This article will show you how to properly and safely install a wall safe to secure your valuables.
== Steps ==

# Locate your studs. You will want to fix your safe to a stud or between studs. This means their location and distance from one another will determine where you put your safe and how large it should be.
#* Use a stud finder to locate the studs behind the wall.
#* If you don’t have a stud finder you can knock on the wall and listen for a hollow or solid sound.
# Choose a safe. Now that you know where you are going to place your safe you can choose one that has the correct size and depth.

#* Match grading systems and content recommendations with what you intend to put into your safes. For instance, you can look at UL safe certifications or the Eurograde system to make sure you have a safe that can ideally hold your valuables.
#* Measure the intended section of wall and look at the safe’s dimensions to be sure it will fit.
#* Think about what kind of entry you want. Digital codes, combination dials, key locks and even fingerprint scanning are all options to consider.

# Make the first cut. After you’ve found a good safe and a place to install it between studs, you are ready to cut into your wall. There are many tools that can do this job but this largely depends on the type of wall you intend to install your safe onto. If it is drywall a drywall saw works well.
#* Make a small cut first. A small hole will allow you to see inside your wall without doing too much damage.
#* Look for electrical wiring and plumbing. If you find wires you need to be extra careful. If you can, go around them or reroute them. If you find plumbing in the way your options are more limited.
#* If something is in the way and you are not confident in your ability to safely move or go around it, the best option is to find a new section of wall.
#* If the wall is clear, you are ready to cut out a space for your safe.
# Measure, measure, measure! Before you make the final cuts in your wall, be sure to carefully measure and trace the cut. Don’t leave yourself with an uneven whole or one that is the wrong size.
#* The hole should be close enough to a stud so that you can attach it to your safe later.
#* Use measuring tape and a pencil to mark each corner of your square hole.
#* Use a ruler or another straight edge to connect each corner.

#* Finally, use a leveler to make sure your square won’t cause your safe to be installed diagonally. The top and bottom should be parallel with the ground while the sides are parallel with your studs.
#* When the hole is cut, slide your safe into place.

# Fix your safe to the studs. This is an important step that prevents burglars from simply cutting your safe out of the wall and walking away with the whole things. The method you use to fix your safe to the studs depends on what those studs are made of.
#* Mark where the holes in your safe line up with your studs with a pencil or a marker.
#* Remove the safe to drill small starter holes. This will make it easier to drill in the screws, especially into more durable materials.
#* Put the safe back in and line up the holes.
#* Drill in each screw and then tighten them firmly.
== Tips ==
* Avoid walls near electrical and plumbing fixtures that may house wiring or pipes.
* Things you will need:
* Stud Finder (if necessary)
*  Pencil
* Measuring Tape or Ruler
* Spirit Level
* Power Drill
== Warnings ==
* Installing a wall safe can be quick and painless. However, if you have little handiwork experience, consult an experienced (and trusted) handyman.
